subject: On‑prem verification checklist + fallback playbook for Aug 28 cutover
messages:
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, ops@acme.io
Cc: procure@vendorcorp.com
Date: 2026-08-26T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: On‑prem verification checklist + fallback playbook for Aug 28 cutover

Team / Acme ops —

We’re two days out from the scheduled VPC/on‑prem cutover window (Sat 08/28 02:00–06:00 UTC). I put together a short verification checklist and a minimal fallback playbook so the ops crew has clear steps if we need to roll back. Please confirm you have the attachments (runbook‑v2.pdf) and can ack the key readiness gates below before EOD Friday (26 Aug).

Readiness gates (quick):
- Network VLANS and transit routes: validated by Acme (netmap attached)
- K/V cache priming: prewarming script executed in staging, route parity checked
- TLS certs: procured and vended to on‑prem LB (expiry > 90d)
- Monitoring probes: Datadog probes + synthetic traces configured on 1s cadence
- Rollback channel: established Slack #acme-cutover and escalation warroom phone tree (see runbook appendix)

Fallback playbook (short):
1) If >10% 5xx across p50 latency within first 15m, pause new traffic on Edge LB;
2) Redirect traffic to Hosted fallback (redwood-hosted-model‑v1) via routing policy (jonas will trigger);
3) If hotfix required, promote hotpatch build and drain nodes;
4) If network fabric issue persists beyond 60m, initiate staged rollback documented in section 5 of runbook.

Attachments: runbook‑v2.pdf (contains commands, verification scripts), network‑mapping‑ansi.txt

Marissa / Jonas — can you confirm the route to promote hosted fallback is tested and you’re comfortable with the 15m detection window? Acme ops — can you confirm you’ll run the smoke list from the attachment and post results to the Drive link?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, ops@acme.io
Date: 2026-08-26T17:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem verification checklist + fallback playbook for Aug 28 cutover

Ack — I pulled the runbook and added a short preflight play to the start (section 1.1). Highlights:
- Preflight commands (local): ./scripts/preflight_check.sh --targets acme-edge
- KV priming: priming completed in staging with 95th percentile latency under threshold
- Routing promotion: jonas and I validated the hosted fallback PR in the lab using traffic mirroring (see smoke‑results‑20260827.csv)

Minor note: the current LB config keeps the existing keepalive at 30s; I recommend 60s for the first 2h post‑cutover to reduce churn during initial scaling. I added that to the runbook appendix.

Attaching smoke results and a tiny diff for the runbook. Will be on the bridge for the window.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: ops@acme.io
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@vendorcorp.com
Date: 2026-08-27T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem verification checklist + fallback playbook for Aug 28 cutover

Karthik / Marissa —

Acme ops confirms: network VLANS validated against network‑mapping‑ansi.txt; transit route flapping observed on a single peering (Edge‑peer‑7) during the 03:00–03:15 simulated load test. We ran the smoke list and included the results in Drive. Summary: most checks green, 1 failing hop (packet loss ~4% for 30s). We cleared the neighbor after we bumped the MTU on the transit interface; will revalidate Sat morning before the window.

We will staff the 02:00–08:00 UTC window with two on‑site network engineers and one sysops lead. If we need a rollback, we will flag in Slack and call the warroom phone tree.

—Acme Ops
Ops Team, Acme Logistics
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ops@acme.io
Date: 2026-08-28T02:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem verification checklist + fallback playbook for Aug 28 cutover

On the bridge now — starting staged traffic shift (step 0)

Live notes:
- 02:12 UTC: drift detected in LB config; automated policy fixed config in 18s (no impact)
- 02:25 UTC: KV cache priming succeeded, 99.9% warm hit for the first sample set
- 02:34 UTC: small burst of 502s from inference nodes (total 1.8% traffic) — scaling triggered, p50 latency rose from 85ms to 240ms for 90s
- 02:38 UTC: promoted hosted fallback for 12% of traffic (test cohort) — observed immediate reduction in 502s and latencies stabilized

Action: continuing slow ramp to 50% and monitoring SLOs. If errors cross 5% sustained over 5m, we will execute full rollback per runbook section 5.

—Jonas
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai, ops@acme.io
Cc: procure@vendorcorp.com
Date: 2026-08-28T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem verification checklist + fallback playbook for Aug 28 cutover — summary

Final summary and next steps:

- Cutover status: partial activation completed; 50% traffic on on‑prem, 50% on hosted fallback. No customer‑visible degradation after the cohort split.
- Issues observed: transient 502 spike during initial ramp tied to a mis‑set keepalive header (Marissa flagged; fixed to 60s).
- Remediations performed: kept fallback active for 10% of traffic for 2h as a safety buffer; on‑site Acme network engineer revalidated peering after MTU change.
- Postcutover ops: run smoke suite again in 1h and attach results to Drive; leave hosted fallback route in place until healthy metrics at 24h.

Thanks to everyone for crisp execution. I’ll open a short post‑cut review doc (5–10 mins read) with timestamps and action items for the retrospective.

Karthik
